html:
Zabutodask (J53)

Survey-table region: Forbidden Plains.

In a sentence: Rise from the Lake Federation's breakup and the memory of the steppe, and use cavalry, firearms, and a new theology to decide the future of the steppe peoples.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (35 J53-exclusive definitions; shared Lake Federation content is additional) | Mission-tree update: based on local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: High | Tedium: Medium (formation requirements and later steppe governance) | Early pressure: varies by predecessor and breakup situation | Expansion: High

Identity and history

The current in-game Chinese name translates as “Great Riders,” while the authoritative English country name is Zabutodask; this is not a separate country. J53 has a country-history template for Zabatlari culture, an oligarchic republic, and the Kodave faith, but the base game does not make it a fixed landholding country in 1444. It is a later formation route within the Lake Federation system. The template's capital and government must not be projected backward as an independent 1444 state. 【Local script】【Local Chinese localisation】

The Zabatlari of the Lake Federation, memories of the steppe, and the Orachav riders form its background. The offline Wiki's “Lake Federation” article describes the Orachav as a mixed people returning from the lakes to their ancestral steppe and restoring the Yudunyovi faith; however, that passage concerns the much later Kalsyto era and cannot be treated as J53's history in 1444. The current missions and events are the main narrative evidence for this player route. 【Wiki】【Local narrative text】

From Federation breakup to steppe republic

The current scripts bring some Lake Federation members into the conditions for the Federation's breakup: J23, J24, and J25 can become J53 when the relevant triggers are met. The formation effect changes the Tag and replaces the mission tree with the Great Riders' missions. This is not the Lake Federation J33's ordinary unification, and the Federation's entire earlier mission tree should not be presented as exclusive J53 content. The formation year depends on the campaign and triggers; it is not a fixed historical date. 【Local script】

The opening exclusive missions address a practical question: after leaving the lakeside cities, how can steppe land sustain people and horses? “People and Nature” concerns pastoralism and steppe governance, while “People and Others” turns Cossack military organisation into state institutions. A republic cannot rely on cavalry charges alone; its frontier must remain viable in peacetime too. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

Core mechanics and later choices

The middle “Rebirth of the Pantheon” arc reorganises ancestors, the sun, and steppe beliefs into the language of state politics. The later “Firearms on Horseback” arc combines cavalry tradition with the adoption of firearms. Expansion into the Forbidden Plains and Bulwar requires managing water, pasture, and new subjects. Ordinary firearms here are not an artificer mechanic, so the country's magic/artifice theme intensity should not be inflated merely because it uses guns. 【Local script】

The sharpest choice comes after the centaurs have been pushed back. Event text explicitly offers reconciliation or extermination: one route attempts to end reciprocal reprisals, while the other continues to hunt down fleeing centaurs. This optional branch determines the country's values; the unchosen outcome is not part of its established history. A later expedition into Bulwar is likewise a mission-tree future, not evidence that the Lake Federation already ruled the south in 1444. 【Local narrative text】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 90/100 | Autocracy 42/100 | Magic–Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 20/100) | Pluralism 55/100. Alternative phase profiles, not a compulsory sequence: reconciliation (Pluralism 75) or extermination (Pluralism 5).

The v2.1 values assessment is Neutral (54/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. These are alternative outcomes, not a compulsory sequence: centaur reconciliation (Good, 76/100) or centaur extermination (Evil, 8/100). Steppe livelihoods, republican government, and the option of peace serve the public good; the other optional route explicitly pursues fleeing centaurs and gravely denies their personhood. The lower-confidence combined score does not equate the routes morally: the results card presents the two alternatives separately. In the reconciliation outcome, ending reprisals benefits steppe governance; in the extermination outcome, pursuing the refugees gravely harms dignity, personhood, and restraint. Cavalry conquest alone is not evidence of good or evil. The branch-specific values profiles are Good (76/100) for reconciliation and Evil (8/100) for extermination.

Recommended for players who enjoy an alternate Lake Federation ending, cavalry and firearms, steppe governance, and consequential moral choices. If you only want a stable Federation-unification campaign, or do not want to face a potentially very dark centaur ending, do not treat this as a routine upgraded Federation.

Community experience and evidence boundary

The early Lake Federation Dev Diary explains the Federation's institutions, not J53 directly. Player posts from 2023–2024 discuss how to trigger the breakup and why Federation missions may still appear after formation; these are development-branch/older-version experiences, so the current entry point is determined by the scripts. 【Related official Dev Diary】【Community opinion】

The offline Wiki has no readable dedicated J53 country page; the related page read here provides steppe background only. See the evidence page for formation scripts, localisation, event text, and discussion links.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Zabutodask (J53) — Orachav Ideas

Set ID: J53_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J53
    }

Orachav Traditions

  • global_regiment_cost：-10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • shock_damage_received：-15% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.15).

1. Nomads of the Plains

While the modern Triunics may appear otherwise, the Zabatlari were once numerous nomadic groups that lived across the entire steppe. While many techniques have since been forgotten, the capacity to recover them has lingered in our blood. With those adventurous at heart joining us to forge a new identity on the plains as the Orachav, it is only a matter of time before the lands belong to us again.

  • Movement speed: +15% (movement_speed; raw value 0.15).

2. Old Sun Rising

While the goddesses of the lakes are closely associated with the Triunics, they were not the first gods worshiped by our people. Inscribed on ruins across the endless grasslands are the rites of our forefathers, and highest among them are those towards Taqoshur, the sun above our heads and the source of all life and civilization. While it was behind mother Yukel's waves that we bided our time, it is under Taqoshur's glow that we face our destiny head-on.

  • Missionary strength: +2% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.02).

3. Mounted Warfare

While the forests, hills, and cities of Leloyal inhibited the movements of cavalry, the open steppe demands the free movement only a mount can provide. While we have yet to master this form, you need only look to a pack of centaurs to learn the role of mobility in combat. To have your enemy surrounded is to have effectively won a battle before it has even begun, and to retain the ability to flee from an advancing foe ensures total defeat is an impossibility. Let no Orachav fight with their feet upon the ground, and they will never be vanquished.

  • Land leader maneuver: +1 (leader_land_manuever; raw value 1).

  • Cavalry flanking ability: +50% (cavalry_flanking; raw value 0.50).

4. Aid the Blessed Warrior

As we reclaim our own ancestral lands from those that took it from us, the stout inhabitants of the mountains surrounding us have begun to do the same. Tayoghor, a god of such proportions, embodies this desire to protect our lands from that which threaten it, and to enrich ourselves from the bounty of our land. Any who fight against the forces of evil and disaster are a friend to the Orachav, and any skilled warrior can find a home among us.

  • Adventurer loyalty equilibrium: +10% (adventurers_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Core-creation cost: -10% (core_creation; raw value -0.1).

5. Well Traveled Armies

When a lone Orachav travels, knowing how much food to carry can be a matter of life and death, for the nearest supplies could be days away. When a group travels, herd animals may be brought along, but in the haste of war this luxury cannot be afforded. While horses can tilt their necks and feast upon grass at a moment's notice, our men must be prepared for weeks of travel and know how to prepare for it.

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +25% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.25).

6. Qultiqatish

While the physically stronger centaur has been the master of hectic warfare, the introduction of the firearm has returned the advantage to us. Their charges across the field of battle mean little now that we can drop them dead from a distance, which we can maintain upon our own steeds. While some have learned to fire a bow from atop a horse, the effectiveness of the gun will multiply that technique tenfold.

  • Cavalry Fire: +50% (cavalry_fire; raw value 0.5).

7. Adoptive Warfare

Yerush teaches us that while the lands of the steppe may be consistent, the wars needed to defend it are anything but. When terrain is not limited, the formations of friend and foe alike. The flares and smoke of our fellow men's Budakh Brigades, the endless harassment of a centaur Taryean Raider party, or the Ogrish bulk of an Armed Iklomgemar, we must be prepared to adapt to and vanquish them all.

  • Free Military Policies: +1 (free_mil_policy; raw value 1).

Orachav Ambition

  • Subject liberty desire: +1000% (reduced_liberty_desire; raw value 10).

Yikashlay (J23) — Yikashlayi Ideas

Set ID: J23_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J23
    }

Yikashlayi Traditions

  • Fort defense: +10% (defensiveness; raw value 0.1).

  • Tolerance of heretics: +2 (tolerance_heretic; raw value 2).

1. Fertilizing our Fields

When the Great Incursion reached our city the centaurs met their match, our city being built atop a great plateau that they could not scale. Even faced with such an obstacle they, perhaps admirably, persisted, leaving thousands of their warriors slain by our archers below our towers. Thanks to their stubbornness we have plenty of materiel to fertilize our fields with.

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

2. Legacy of "He of the Horizon"

Yikashlay was founded by a mysterious sorcerer known as "He of the Horizon", who raised the plateau our city rests upon and constructing many of the towers our people call home. Quite a few of the towers are still barely used, allowing us to convert them to whatever purposes we require.

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Hanging Gardens of Yikashlay

The centaur hordes must have been attempting to starve us out of our towers. How they must have wept when we simply began growing our produce from our tallest towers.

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

4. Yikashlayi Diplomacy

There are those that would call our dignitaries "vulgar" and "crude", but it is they that simply cannot take a goodnatured joke.

  • Power projection from insults: +1 (power_projection_from_insults; raw value 1).

5. Hill Market

As our plateau runs out of space to construct towers upon and our standing edifices fill with workshops and residences, we have taken to expanding into the rock beneath our city, establishing a bustling market carved within the very bedrock.

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

6. Charting the Stars

Our city offers a view like none other, granting an unobstructed view of the stars above at night, which our scholars have taken to meticulously tracking and charting.

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

7. Scraping the Skies

Our towers are full, and the land beneath risks collapsing should we carve any further. We have only one way to expand; to the very clouds above our towers.

  • Build time: -20% (build_time; raw value -0.2).

Yikashlayi Ambition

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

Zabyos'tlar (J24) — Zabyos'tlaric Ideas

Set ID: J24_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J24
    }

Zabyos'tlaric Traditions

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

1. Rebuilding the West End

The western half of our city was utterly devastated by the centaur hordes during the Great Incursion. Much work must be done to return prosperity to this district.

  • Construction cost: -5% (build_cost; raw value -0.05).

  • Development cost: -5% (development_cost; raw value -0.05).

2. Sovkokeya

The Sovkokeya is the most commonly used trade ship in Lake Yukelqur, prized for its spacious hold capable of carrying trade goods and men alike.

  • Ship trade power propagation: +20% (ship_power_propagation; raw value 0.2).

  • Embarkation and Disembarkation Movement Speed Modifier: +10% (movement_speed_onto_off_boat_modifier; raw value 0.1).

3. Canal Marines

To keep smugglers from choking our canal we've organized a militia of marines to patrol the banks. In times of war we can assign these marines to bolster our naval forces.

  • Sailor Modifier: +20% (global_sailors_modifier; raw value 0.2).

  • Marine force limit: +10% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.1).

4. Office of Mercenary Affairs

The O.M.A. is an organization dedicated to ensuring our hired blades are doing the jobs they were hired for to the best of their ability, and spend their earnings on improving their equipment rather than on drink and women. While some may see this as overbearing our budget certainly appreciates it.

  • Mercenary Maintenance: -20% (merc_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.2).

5. The Sky Walk

As our city expands we have taken to constructing great towers linked with bridges crossing over the canal, our wealthy have packed up and moved to this soaring district and many merchants choose to spend long periods of shore leave within the establishments gracing the Sky Walk.

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

6. Tlaric Gangs

While our city soars, those left below, quite literally in the dark, toil within the polluted detritus of our undercity. While they may be rowdy brutes, they do bring a certain set of skills to our militia.

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

7. Guild of the Lightbearers

To guide ships through our now darkened canal, the Lightbearers carry torches along the way. They act as our enforcers within the undercity, keeping the scum and rabble out of sight from visiting traders.

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

Zabyos'tlaric Ambition

  • Galley Combat Ability: +10% (galley_power; raw value 0.1).

Buruvaqoyla (J25) — Buruvaqoylan Ideas

Set ID: J25_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = J25
    }

Buruvaqoylan Traditions

  • Mercenary Cost: -20% (mercenary_cost; raw value -0.2).

  • Mercenary Discipline: +5% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.05).

1. Home of the Jolgik Ut

Buruvaqoyla plays host to the legendary mercenary band, the Jolgik Uts. Originally exiles from the islands sent to die fighting the centaurs, since our city's founding they've become a disciplined and respected force of centaur slayers.

  • shock_damage_received：-10% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.1).

2. Life on the Frontline

Every man must be ready to take up arms and fend off the centaur raids that plague our hinterlands on a yearly basis. Such is life so close to the hordelands.

  • Reinforce cost: -10% (reinforce_cost_modifier; raw value -0.1).

3. Pushing the Frontier

With the backing of the Federation, we can finally extend our reach beyond our borders into the old lands of our forefathers, taking back the lands our ancestors were forced to flee when the centaurs bore down on them.

  • Core-creation cost: -5% (core_creation; raw value -0.05).

  • Movement speed: +10% (movement_speed; raw value 0.1).

4. Beauty in Chaos

When one has but a moment's rest to admire the land around them, they can fully recognize the serene and comforting landscape we find ourselves in. If we must fall, we cannot imagine a more scenic place to do so.

  • Prestige: +1 (prestige; raw value 1).

5. Lady of Buruvaqoyla

The Jolgik Uts that founded our city were led by the legendary Lady of Buruvaqoyla. Her origins are a mystery, some claim she was but a former bandit from the northern cities, others suggest that she was a disinherited princess. Whatever her background truly was, we are determined to ensure her dream never falls.

  • Fort defense: +10% (defensiveness; raw value 0.1).

6. Turning the Tables

We finally have the opportunity to subject the dreaded centaurs to the horrors they've inflicted upon us for so long, hunting them in their homes and razing their villages as they did so many times to our hinterlands.

  • Cavalry combat ability: +15% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.15).

7. Taming the Plains

The Forbidden Plains are vast, a seemingly endless expanse of grass and sand. Led by our fearless Jolgik Uts, our armies have learned to navigate this land like no other.

  • Army attrition: -10% (land_attrition; raw value -0.1).

Buruvaqoylan Ambition

  • Mercenary Maintenance: -20% (merc_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.2).
